claim_under_test: Returning the withheld FINE_GUARD_SAMPLES on every abort path makes the delivered grid land on the coarse formula instead of sixteen samples short.
result: Confirmed on hardware. Every capture now shows two resync skips: the coarse one at formula minus sixteen and a late fine one of exactly sixteen. Their total equals the formula exactly on all five captures, against minus sixteen on eleven of eleven before the fix.
still_open: The joint estimate itself is still declined - the search continues to hit a history read miss - so the grid degrades to coarse-only rather than being refined. The fine skip also lands around trace entry 53, far past the header, so it cannot help the symbols decoded before it.

read_miss_root_cause.finding: The abort is the search outliving the history retention of its own read region, reported at the exact cycle the write pointer reaches that region.
read_miss_root_cause.mechanism: lora_iq_history_buffer raises read_miss for two different things: a sample outside [oldest, next), and read_write_collision, which is read_addr == write_addr on a cycle when a sample arrives. The joint search reads a fixed window 9.75 symbols behind the write pointer. While it runs, the write pointer advances; after a full 65536-sample wrap it reaches that window, the collision fires, read_miss feeds search_failed, and the joint estimate is abandoned.

quantitative_confirmation.model: samples from trace start to the fine skip = DEPTH - lookback + coarse_advance
quantitative_confirmation.residual: fine_skip_at_sample minus coarse_advance equals 55552 on all five captures with zero residual, so the slope against the advance is exactly 1. DEPTH minus that constant is 9984 samples, 9.75 symbols, which is the lookback from the write pointer to the read window at search start.

read_miss_root_cause.supersedes: This replaces the earlier future-read conclusion. That was reached by elimination - a too-old read is impossible so soon after the stream reset - but the elimination missed a third cause, the collision. The up-search data-ready wait added on the strength of it is correct and harmless, but it was not the fix.
read_miss_root_cause.open: Why the search is still running after fifty-four symbols. The packet-rate RTL regression measures the pair at 135,443 clocks, about two symbols. Twenty-five times that on hardware is the next thing to explain, and it is what makes the read window age out at all.

search_duration_measured.question: Is the joint search slow on hardware, or does it merely start late? The abort timing alone cannot tell the two apart.
search_duration_measured.method: toa_search_busy is status bit 4. The sampling loop runs on the board rather than over SSH: each devmem is a process spawn of about a millisecond, which separates 2 ms from 56 ms, whereas an SSH round trip per sample would not.
search_duration_measured.conclusion: The search is genuinely slow, not late. Hardware holds toa_search_busy for 40 to 70 ms against 2.17 ms in simulation, which is roughly 37 clocks per tap instead of 2. That duration is what lets the read window age out at 56 ms, so the slowness is the cause and the collision is the symptom.
search_duration_measured.eliminated: STATE_WAIT_DOWN_DATA is one clock in the full-receiver probe, so the controller does not wait there. packet_start_valid pulses once, so there is no repeated retriggering. The joint-path regression measures the identical 135,443 clocks whether the sample stream is frozen, dense or paced at the real 63 clocks per sample, so the search duration does not depend on sample pacing either.
search_duration_measured.next: Why a tap costs about 37 clocks on hardware and 2 in simulation. The MAC aborts on the first iq_read_miss rather than grinding through misses, and response_mismatch_error is clear, so neither explains it. Settling this needs visibility into the MAC state on hardware.
